texts.title: Fables 1–53
texts.author: Aesop
texts.description: Chambry's text of the first fifty-three fables. Short, repetitive, and each one finishes in a sitting. Hand-annotated, with contextual word glosses from the Perseus annotators.

texts.title: Dialogues of the Gods
texts.author: Lucian
texts.description: Twenty-five short comic dialogues. Conversational Attic and the dialogue form before Plato. Automatic parse (GLAUx), so the structure view can be wrong in places.

texts.title: Dialogues of the Dead
texts.author: Lucian
texts.description: Thirty dialogues set in the underworld. Automatic parse (GLAUx).

texts.title: Anabasis, Book 1
texts.author: Xenophon
texts.description: Plain narrative prose with syntax close to Plutarch's; the traditional first author. Hand-annotated by Vanessa Gorman.

texts.title: Gospel of John
texts.author: John
texts.description: The easiest Greek prose there is, but Koine rather than Attic: an optional detour. PROIEL treebank, translation by verse (KJV).

texts.title: Life of Lycurgus
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.description: Sparta's lawgiver. Long periodic sentences built from participles.

texts.title: Life of Alcibiades
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.description: The most novelistic of the Lives.

texts.title: Euthyphro
texts.author: Plato
texts.description: Socrates outside the court, on what piety is. The target text: the progress figure on the library page is computed against it.
